name: AZ-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 4 points and the favorable national environment adds to it
Incumbent Greg Stanton is running with a large cash advantage ($2.0M vs $0.3M)
Prediction markets price Stanton at about 97% to win
No public polling, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Stanton combines a Democratic-leaning seat, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge over Zuhdi Jasser, while markets price the race as effectively decided. With no polling to contradict the fundamentals, the race stays in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late public polling showing a much tighter race or a surge of outside spending against Stanton would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Greg Stanton seeks a fourth term in a Phoenix-area district that leans Democratic by about four points. He has raised over $2.1 million and holds roughly $2 million on hand, while Republican Zuhdi Jasser has raised about $565,000 with a fraction of that cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against Stanton, and prediction markets give him roughly a 97% chance of winning.

With no public general-election polling available, the race is judged on fundamentals: the district lean, a favorable environment for Democrats, incumbency, and Stanton's financial advantage all point the same direction. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot but is not a significant factor. The race is rated Safe Democratic.
